Argentina Imposes Temporary Tariff on Foreign Banking Software, Impacting Local Banks

The Argentine government has imposed a temporary 15% tariff on the import of foreign banking software and digital infrastructure, a move officials say is intended to protect and stimulate domestic development in the sector. The measure, which took effect last week, applies to all new purchases and upgrades of core banking systems, cybersecurity platforms, and digital banking solutions sourced from abroad.

The immediate effects have been felt by several banks operating in Argentina, with institutions reporting delays in digital service rollouts and increased operational costs. “We are reviewing our technology investment plans for the year,” said Lucía Menéndez, spokesperson for Banco Patria, “as the new tariff significantly increases the cost of upgrading our mobile banking app.” 

Banking industry representatives have voiced concern over the measure’s timing. “This tariff introduces uncertainty for banks already investing heavily in digital transformation,” said Esteban Rivas, president of the Argentine Association of Banking Institutions. “We are monitoring the situation closely and are in dialogue with authorities to minimize disruption for our clients and staff.”

Several banks have paused hiring for IT and digital operations roles, citing cost pressures and uncertainty around future technology investments. At the same time, bank branches in Buenos Aires and Córdoba have reported slower deployment of new digital kiosks and self-service terminals, according to local union figures.

Government officials have signaled the measure will be reviewed after an initial 90-day period. In the meantime, banking firms are assessing ways to accelerate the adoption of locally-developed software and exploring interim solutions to maintain service continuity. The situation remains fluid as stakeholders await further guidance.
